clue.text: Undemanding theatre is a warning in the main

parts.note: light reading or light duties are undemanding
a theatre is a playhouse, often just called a house

explanation.surface: An easy-going playhouse is somehow also an alert out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower with a beam exists to warn ships of danger at sea.

clue.text: Crime, for example, recalled damage by fire

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a moral crime

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A list of examples of crime, remembered alongside fire damage.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch something lightly is to damage it by fire, a close synonym.

clue.text: Glance at telly, losing heart, having little coverage

parts.note: to scan a page is to glance at it quickly

indicators.note: the heart of the word telly is its middle letters, which go

explanation.surface: Someone glancing at a TV programme that seems to have lost its spirit and has thin coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' strips the middle ELL from TELLY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing is skimpy, covering little of the body.

clue.text: Posh fellow losing head? That's not on

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for the posh fellow is dropped

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class man

explanation.surface: An upper-class man loses his temper, and someone says that is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' doubles as 'that is unacceptable' and the literal opposite of on.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch that is not on is in its opposite position, the antonym state.

clue.text: Bloomer in award for dairymen?

definitions.meaning: a bloomer here is something that blooms, a flower, rather than a blunder or loaf
a whimsical trophy for those who make dairy produce, a cup for butter

explanation.surface: A blunder made when handing out a prize to dairy farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow meadow flower is a bloomer; read in two words it names a trophy for churning.

clue.text: Opening of file (more ancient file)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: older means more ancient

explanation.surface: A note about the start of an older document in a filing system.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'file' only gives its first letter; the second, in brackets, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard holder for papers is a file in an office.

clue.text: OT prophet uneasily in lead

indicators.note: uneasily suggests something unsettled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Old Testament seer leading the way with some unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' shuffles the letters of IN LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Daniel is in the Old Testament, and its hero is a prophet.

clue.text: Taxi-man, scoundrel cornering Bishop beside Thames?

indicators.note: beside puts the next piece right after the first
cornering means trapping, so the scoundrel's letters enclose the bishop

parts.note: a cad is an old word for a dishonourable man
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the Thames is the river through London

explanation.surface: A London cabbie, a rogue who traps a bishop by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cornering' puts B inside CAD to give CABD.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi-man is someone who drives a cab for a living.

clue.text: Bill volunteers to get billions

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army
b is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: An invoice for volunteers who are set to earn billions.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar tab is the running bill you settle at the end of the night.

clue.text: Cricket official's heart lying in beginning to smash runs

indicators.note: lying in means sitting inside the letters around it
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the core of something is its heart

explanation.surface: A cricket official whose heart lies in big hitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in' puts CORE between S, the start of 'smash', and R for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the person who records the runs and wickets is an official of the game.

clue.text: Farewell to the French, about to depart

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French words wrap around the next piece

parts.note: au is French for to the
to die is to depart this life

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to the French just before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the French' is not part of the definition: it asks for the French words for 'to the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French word is a goodbye, used for a final parting.

clue.text: Jumping sheep delay one dropping off

indicators.note: jumping suggests the letters leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: Counting jumping sheep holds up someone trying to fall asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping' rearranges SHEEP DELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping off is nodding to sleep, and a drowsy person does just that.

clue.text: Humiliation for watchmaker?

definitions.meaning: public humiliation, a blow to one's standing
a watchmaker's mishap would be the dial of a watch going missing

explanation.surface: Asking what embarrassment means to a watchmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a watch's dial is its face.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a damaging dent in pride and reputation.

clue.text: Win, after disposing of a drink of spirits

indicators.note: after disposing of says the following word is thrown out

parts.note: to gain is to win

explanation.surface: After a victory, someone gets rid of a glass of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after disposing of' removes A from GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The juniper-flavoured spirit is a classic alcoholic drink.

clue.text: High singer capturing music's first quaver

indicators.note: capturing means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano, a high voice

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A boy soprano catching the first quaver of the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quaver' looks like a musical note; here it is a verb, to shake.
explanation.definitionFit: To quaver is to shake or quiver, as a nervous voice does.

clue.text: One holds position at one's place of work

indicators.note: holds means the word one contains the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
to sit something is to position or place it

explanation.surface: Someone holds a post right where they work.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at the workplace itself, rather than off-premises or remotely.

clue.text: Stone Age period

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: The prehistoric era named after stone tools.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is a phase or period in a process of development.

clue.text: Shopkeeper's standard is foremost in trading

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard, as in a stock answer

indicators.note: foremost in picks the very first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's usual habit is to put trading first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopkeeper's' reads as 'shopkeeper is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer who keeps a particular brand on its shelves is a seller of those goods.

clue.text: Period certain to have you transfixed

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A spell of time sure to hold you riveted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have you' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entranced or held motionless with fascination is a close synonym.

clue.text: Footballer's well-fed sponsor

parts.note: someone well-fed is full
to back a venture is to sponsor it

explanation.surface: A footballer's sponsor who has eaten well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footballer's' reads as 'footballer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender playing near the goal is a position in football.

clue.text: Previously a pound cash

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
the ready is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: In the past, a pound was a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' or 'readies' is British slang for cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by now or before the expected time means earlier, before this point.

clue.text: Disinclined to claim state is heartless

parts.note: to aver is to claim or assert

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of the word state

explanation.surface: Unwilling to claim the government is cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle TAT from STATE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to or unwilling to do something is reluctant, disinclined.

clue.text: Rustic river, Russian river

parts.note: the Ural flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A countrified river scene in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means of the countryside, the plain synonym for country-like.

clue.text: Wintry stuff that is getting cold inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Winter weather that grows cold inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts C into IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is the archetypal wintry substance.
